scholarly_summaries.translated_summary: Relevance of the Topic. Ukrainian sacred art has long occupied a prominent place in national culture. The Church and its creative inspirations, especially in the early modern era, were an important factor in the formation and development of artistic progress, and in this a great role belongs to the sphere of liturgical chant. The core of the Ukrainian church chant tradition is monophony, or the ancient medieval monodic practice, whose roots reach back to Byzantine liturgical rite. Thus, sacred monody is evidence of continuity and, at the same time, a solid foundation for the development of the national spiritual art. With the introduction of polyphony into liturgical practice, monody did not lose its significance and remained the basis of the divine services of the daily cycle, which begins with Vespers. Therefore, the study of the chant repertoire of Vespers is relevant first of all from the standpoint of the historical reconstruction of the foundations of Ukrainian liturgical rite. As a result of the reform of notation—the introduction of the five-line form of notation—innovative staff-notated liturgical collections emerged in early modern Ukraine, namely the irmologia, which also included the repertoire of Vespers. A precise reading of these chants makes it possible to obtain an authentic record of the chant palette of the sacred rite. All this allows us to reconstruct a real picture of the Vespers service of the Baroque era in the context of the artistic significance of church life, the study of which is relevant for various reasons. ## Sunday of Pentecost

1. The Service of this Feast is celebrated over seven days, for it has its Apodosis on the coming Saturday. scholarly_summaries.study_title: Kyivan Chant in the Context of 17th–18th Century Irmologia
scholarly_summaries.translated_summary: The main branch of Ukrainian church monody - Kyiv chant - has more than a thousand years of history of existence. Its origins date back to the period of the official acceptance of Christianity by Kievan Rus' at the end of the 10th century, and possibly even to the 9th century when the first Christian churches appeared in Kyiv. In the middle of the 11th century, with the division of the Universal Church into Eastern and Western, Kyiv chant (of course, it did not have this name then) was definitively established as a branch of Slavic vocal art in the Orthodox Greek-Byzantine area. From its inception, the tradition has been continuous: strengthening or weakening, it constantly revived and acquired new qualities in different epochs.

scholarly_summaries.study_title: The Liturgical and Musical Dimension of Great Vespers in Ukrainian Irmologia
scholarly_summaries.translated_summary: Relevance of the Topic. Ukrainian sacred art has long occupied a prominent place in national culture. The core of the Ukrainian church chant tradition is monophony, or the ancient medieval monodic practice, whose roots reach back to Byzantine liturgical rite. Thus, sacred monody is evidence of continuity and, at the same time, a solid foundation for the development of the national spiritual art. With the introduction of polyphony into liturgical practice, monody did not lose its significance and remained the basis of the divine services of the daily cycle, which begins with Vespers. Therefore, the study of the chant repertoire of Vespers is relevant first of all from the standpoint of the historical reconstruction of the foundations of Ukrainian liturgical rite. As a result of the reform of notation—the introduction of the five-line form of notation—innovative staff-notated liturgical collections emerged in early modern Ukraine, namely the irmologia, which also included the repertoire of Vespers. A precise reading of these chants makes it possible to obtain an authentic record of the chant palette of the sacred rite. All this allows us to reconstruct a real picture of the Vespers service of the Baroque era in the context of the artistic significance of church life, the study of which is relevant for various reasons. scholarly_summaries.study_title: Computer Database of the East Slavic Heirmologion (Irmos)
scholarly_summaries.translated_summary: Ukrainian, as well as Belarusian, sacred monody is one of the brightest links of the Byzantine cultural space of the early modern era, which for the first time paved the way for rapprochement with New European culture. Already at the end of the sixteenth century, it was precisely in Ukraine and Belarus that, for the first time in the liturgical chant of the Byzantine rite, they fully transitioned to European five-line staff notation for recording musical texts, adapting it to their own practice. The new method of notation not only testified to the significant stylistic evolution of Ukrainian-Belarusian church chant, but also stimulated this process even further. At the same time, the entire repertoire, whose roots went back not only to Kyivan Rus', but also to the Balkan Slavs and, naturally, Byzantium, was transferred to the new system of recording musical text.

scholarly_summaries.translated_summary: The work offered to the reader is the first attempt in Ukrainian historiography to trace the formation of scholarly conceptions of Byzantine hymnography and church monody. ## Sunday of Pentecost

1. The Service of this Feast is celebrated over seven days, for it has its Apodosis on the coming Saturday. It has this proper feature, that on Sunday evening at Vespers toward Monday the Kneeling Prayers are read; and on the morrow, that is, on Monday, the entire Service of the Feast is sung without the Menaion, and at the Liturgy also the Service of the Holy Trinity, if desired,[^658] as we indicate immediately.

All the rest, from the Feast even unto its Apodosis, is performed according to the General Rule of a Feast and Inside a Feast of the Lord. At the Liturgy, **"As many of you as have been baptized into Christ"** (*Є҆ли́цы*), only on the Feast.

scholarly_summaries.study_title: Festal Stikhira Repertoire in Early Modern Ukrainian Heirmologia
scholarly_summaries.translated_summary: The Ukrainian type of Heirmologion as a unified notated liturgical book emerged approximately in the second half of the sixteenth century. Its universality ensured for this type of collection a flexible adaptability to liturgical practice. The Heirmologion also became a unique example of a large-scale all-Ukrainian reform, when, within a short period and literally across all the lands of the Ukrainian ethnos, not only was the optimal chant material selected, but it was also transferred from the ancient znamenny notation to the new five-line staff notation.

scholarly_summaries.study_title: The Liturgical and Musical Dimension of Great Vespers in Ukrainian Irmologia
scholarly_summaries.translated_summary: Relevance of the Topic. Ukrainian sacred art has long occupied a prominent place in national culture. The Church and its creative inspirations, especially in the early modern era, were an important factor in the formation and development of artistic progress, and in this a great role belongs to the sphere of liturgical chant. The core of the Ukrainian church chant tradition is monophony, or the ancient medieval monodic practice, whose roots reach back to Byzantine liturgical rite. Thus, sacred monody is evidence of continuity and, at the same time, a solid foundation for the development of the national spiritual art. With the introduction of polyphony into liturgical practice, monody did not lose its significance and remained the basis of the divine services of the daily cycle, which begins with Vespers. Therefore, the study of the chant repertoire of Vespers is relevant first of all from the standpoint of the historical reconstruction of the foundations of Ukrainian liturgical rite. As a result of the reform of notation—the introduction of the five-line form of notation—innovative staff-notated liturgical collections emerged in early modern Ukraine, namely the irmologia, which also included the repertoire of Vespers. A precise reading of these chants makes it possible to obtain an authentic record of the chant palette of the sacred rite. All this allows us to reconstruct a real picture of the Vespers service of the Baroque era in the context of the artistic significance of church life, the study of which is relevant for various reasons. 1. The Service of this Feast is celebrated over seven days, for it has its Apodosis on the coming Saturday. It has this proper feature, that on Sunday evening at Vespers toward Monday the Kneeling Prayers are read; and on the morrow, that is, on Monday, the entire Service of the Feast is sung without the Menaion, and at the Liturgy also the Service of the Holy Trinity, if desired,[^658] as we indicate immediately.

All the rest, from the Feast even unto its Apodosis, is performed according to the General Rule of a Feast and Inside a Feast of the Lord. At the Liturgy, **"As many of you as have been baptized into Christ"** (*Є҆ли́цы*), only on the Feast.

scholarly_summaries.study_title: Kyivan Chant in the Context of 17th–18th Century Irmologia
scholarly_summaries.translated_summary: The main branch of Ukrainian church monody - Kyiv chant - has more than a thousand years of history of existence. Its origins date back to the period of the official acceptance of Christianity by Kievan Rus' at the end of the 10th century, and possibly even to the 9th century when the first Christian churches appeared in Kyiv. In the middle of the 11th century, with the division of the Universal Church into Eastern and Western, Kyiv chant (of course, it did not have this name then) was definitively established as a branch of Slavic vocal art in the Orthodox Greek-Byzantine area. From its inception, the tradition has been continuous: strengthening or weakening, it constantly revived and acquired new qualities in different epochs.

scholarly_summaries.study_title: Cherubic Hymns of the Suprasl Chant in Staff-Notated Irmologia
scholarly_summaries.translated_summary: The Cherubic Hymn *Izhe kheruvimy* is one of the most important and oldest chants of the Byzantine Church, which from a musical perspective has undergone numerous changes and re-interpretations over a long period. The hymn is sung during the Divine Liturgy, that is, the Liturgy of John Chrysostom, which is the logical conclusion and culmination of the complete daily cycle of liturgical services. Therefore, this hymn is performed practically daily throughout the entire church year, with the exception of certain days of Great Lent. This explains, in particular, the extraordinary popularity of the Cherubic Hymn in composition, from the Baroque era to the present day.

scholarly_summaries.translated_summary: In reality, an immense role in this process belongs to the parish cantor (*diak*) and cantor-teacher (*diako-uchytel*)—a role that is all too infrequently emphasized in our contemporary era. scholarly_summaries.study_title: The Liturgical and Musical Dimension of Great Vespers in Ukrainian Irmologia
scholarly_summaries.translated_summary: Relevance of the Topic. Ukrainian sacred art has long occupied a prominent place in national culture. The Church and its creative inspirations, especially in the early modern era, were an important factor in the formation and development of artistic progress, and in this a great role belongs to the sphere of liturgical chant. The core of the Ukrainian church chant tradition is monophony, or the ancient medieval monodic practice, whose roots reach back to Byzantine liturgical rite. Thus, sacred monody is evidence of continuity and, at the same time, a solid foundation for the development of the national spiritual art. With the introduction of polyphony into liturgical practice, monody did not lose its significance and remained the basis of the divine services of the daily cycle, which begins with Vespers. Therefore, the study of the chant repertoire of Vespers is relevant first of all from the standpoint of the historical reconstruction of the foundations of Ukrainian liturgical rite. As a result of the reform of notation—the introduction of the five-line form of notation—innovative staff-notated liturgical collections emerged in early modern Ukraine, namely the irmologia, which also included the repertoire of Vespers. A precise reading of these chants makes it possible to obtain an authentic record of the chant palette of the sacred rite. All this allows us to reconstruct a real picture of the Vespers service of the Baroque era in the context of the artistic significance of church life, the study of which is relevant for various reasons. On the one hand, Baroque art is evidence of the adaptation of the Byzantine liturgical repertoire and the reinterpretation of its chant forms, and on the other hand, a contemporary vision of the spiritual development of Ukrainian culture is impossible without taking into account the monodic sacred stratum. In this context, Vespers chants are an important continuous link in Ukrainian sacred art, which requires
